title: Talent Activation Handover Playbook — 14d Sprintbox (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a compact 14-day 'Sprintbox' for converting new hires and trial candidates into productive teammates. Designed as a handover between Recruiting -> Hiring Manager -> Mentor -> People Ops. Focus: accelerate signal collection, reduce onboarding friction, and provide a defensible evidence trail for offer/probation decisions.

Audience:
- Hiring managers and interview panel leads
- People Ops and Recruiters
- Assigned mentors and buddy engineers

Summary of flow (one-liner):
Day 0: Handover packet delivered. Days 1–7: focus sprint and signal capture. Days 8–14: consolidation, feedback loop, and decision window.

Key principles (explicit):
- Evidence-first: every decision must reference 2–3 concrete artifacts (code, PRs, recorded pairing notes, task outputs).
- Time-boxed exposure: keep tasks narrowly scoped to reduce cognitive overload and maximize comparable signals.
- Mentor-as-instructor, not assessor: mentors help the candidate demonstrate skills; managerial decision remains separate.
- Compact documentation: use the 1-page evidence ledger template below for each candidate.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Recruiter: assembles Day0 packet, access, hardware, calendar blocks, and success criteria.
- Hiring Manager: defines the 14d sprint goals, approves mentor, and provides role-specific starter task.
- Mentor (peer): runs daily 30-min pairing sessions, updates evidence ledger, and flags risks early.
- People Ops: runs the playbook, triages blockers (tools/accounts), and owns the final decision meeting cadence.

Day0 packet (deliver within 24h of offer acceptance):
- Welcome checklist (IT access + at least 3 service accounts validated)
- 14d sprint brief for candidate (one page): mission, deliverables, evaluation rubric, and top 3 learning resources
- Mentor pairing note: mentor intro script and availability slots
- Evidence ledger template pre-populated with candidate name and recruiter notes

14-day sprint outline (high level):
- Day 0 (preboard): account setup, short intro call (15m) with mentor, deliverables reviewed
- Day 1–3: Onboard context + first micro-task (scoped bug/feature) — goal: finish MVP & open PR
- Day 4–7: Deeper pairing work + handoff of a second micro-task with acceptance criteria — goal: demonstrate iterative workflow and code review participation
- Day 8–10: Cross-functional exposure (brief sessions with docs, infra, SRE as applicable) + candidate writes a 1-page README for their sprint work
- Day 11–13: Consolidation & polish; mentor compiles evidence ledger and writes a short recommendation (2–4 bullets)
- Day 14: Decision sync (Hiring Manager + People Ops + Recruiter + Mentor). Outcome: confirmed, extended trial, or offboard.

Micro-task design rules (for hiring managers):
- Duration: 4–12 hours of focussed work for each micro-task
- Clear acceptance criteria (pass/fail) with at least one measurable outcome (tests, perf, or documented steps)
- Avoid single-vendor proprietary stacks if candidate unfamiliar — prefer representative infra/components they’ll use
- Include at least one code review entry point so we can observe collaboration tone

Evidence ledger (one-line template — captured daily by mentor):
- Day, artifact type (PR/notes/recording), link/filename, observed signals (bullet list), confidence score 1–4, recommended action

Example ledger row:
- Day 3, PR #45, github.com/.../pr/45, "implemented feature X, needed 1 nudge on test structure; responded well to feedback", confidence 3, recommend: proceed

Evaluation rubric (people-ops adapted, normalized 1–4):
- Technical correctness: 4 = reliably correct; 3 = minor fix; 2 = conceptual gaps; 1 = repeated incorrect assumptions
- Collaboration & communication: 4 = proactive, clear, works well with reviewers; 3 = responsive; 2 = needs prompting; 1 = difficult to sync
- Learning velocity: 4 = self-directed & fast; 3 = learns with hints; 2 = slow ramp; 1 = little progress
- Role fit / curiosity: 4 = shows initiative and domain curiosity; 3 = adequate; 2 = limited; 1 = misaligned
- Overall recommended action mapping: average >=3.5 = confirm; 2.5–3.49 = extend trial + growth plan; <2.5 = offboard recommendation

Decision meeting checklist (Day 14):
- People Ops presents evidence ledger (sorted by strongest signals)
- Mentor summarizes top 3 strengths and top 2 blockers (2–3 bullets each)
- Hiring Manager states business need alignment & any capacity concerns
- Recruiter confirms compensation/offer logistics if confirm
- Timestamped decision recorded and candidate informed within 24h

Escalation triggers (immediate flags that require People Ops + Manager intervention):
- Candidate cannot access required accounts after Day 1 despite 2 escalations
- Repeated unresponsiveness across 48 hours without documented reason
- Behavior that violates code of conduct or makes team unsafe

Post-decision hygiene (if confirmed):
- Convert sprint work into onboarding tasks in the new hire’s board (assign owner, due dates)
- 30/60/90 day milestones added to manager 1:1 template
- Mentor shift to long-term buddy with weekly 30m sync for first 6 weeks

If extend trial:
- Define 2-week extension goals with narrower scope and explicit success criteria
- Formal growth plan added to evidence ledger, with check-ins at day +7 of extension

If offboard:
- Offboarding checklist run within 48h, candidate files stored under restricted folder, and recruiter closes loop with courteously phrased note and any severance/compliance steps

Operational notes & traps we've seen (practical):
- Over-scoped tasks lead to poor signal — keep to 8–12 hour tasks max
- Too many observers biases outcomes (panel fatigue). Keep mentors to 1 primary + 1 backup reviewer max for micro-tasks
- Ensure recruiter includes a short competency primer for the mentor; otherwise mentors default to managerial expectations

Mini templates (copy-paste friendly):
- Mentor intro script: "Hi NAME — excited to work with you. Today we'll pair for 30m to align on context, then you’ll take the micro-task. My role is to help you show your skills. If you need anything ping me in #channel or book a 1:1."
- Candidate sprint brief (one-paragraph): "In 14 days you'll complete two micro-tasks representative of day-to-day work. We'll evaluate on technical correctness, collaboration, learning velocity, and role fit. Deliverables: PR for task A, README for sprint, daily short notes. Expect daily 30m pairing with your mentor."

Experiment checklist (people-ops proposed metrics to track across candidates):
- Time to first PR merged (days)
- Evidence ledger completeness score (percent of required rows filled)
- Decision turnaround time (hours between Day14 meeting and candidate notice)
- Conversion rate from Sprintbox -> Full offer (target 70% for mid/sr, 50% for early levels)
- Candidate satisfaction NPS (post-14d)

Open questions & next steps (WIP):
- Should we standardize micro-task templates per role family? (Action: Jonah to prototype for infra/devtools by Nov 22)
- How to treat contractor pipelines differently from perm hires? Quick workshop suggested.
- Integrate with HRIS for automatic 30/60/90 creation on confirm (Mira owns spec)
